What matters when hiring for textile & garments in Tamil Nadu

Tamil Nadu's textile chain is spread across the western districts. Tiruppur leads in knitwear and export garments. Coimbatore and Dindigul have dense spinning mill clusters. Erode and Komarapalayam run powerlooms and processing, and Karur is known for home textiles such as bed linen and curtains. Chennai has export garment units of its own. Pay, hostel facilities and the mix of local and migrant workers differ in each place.

Garment work is paid in several ways: monthly salary, daily wage or piece rate. Operators judge an offer by take-home pay, overtime and hostel facilities, not by the headline salary. Demand rises before export shipment windows and before Deepavali, then drops sharply. A trial on the machine is the only reliable test of a tailor's speed and finish, so we arrange trial stitching wherever the unit allows it.

Buyer social audits look closely at labour practices. Most buyers require every worker to be 18 or older, wages to reach the notified minimum, and overtime to be voluntary and paid at twice the ordinary rate. Hostel workers must be free to leave the premises and keep their own documents. Many buyer codes follow the employer-pays principle, so workers should not pay any recruitment fee.

What we check before sending candidates

  • Arrange a machine trial to check stitching speed and finish
  • Verify age proof so every worker is 18 or older
  • Confirm the worker holds their own ID documents and bank account
  • Explain piece-rate, overtime and hostel terms before joining
  • Check prior mill or unit experience by machine type

Textile & garments hiring: questions employers ask

Can you supply tailors at short notice before a shipment?

Yes, for common machine types such as single needle, overlock and flatlock. First workers arrive within 48 hours for helpers and 7 days for skilled roles, depending on headcount and whether your unit provides hostel space. Tell us the order quantity, garment type and shipment date. Short-notice batches are easier in Tiruppur than in areas with fewer trained tailors.

Will your workers pass a buyer social audit?

We cannot promise an audit result, because it also depends on your working hours, overtime records and hostel conditions. What we can do is supply workers with age proof, ID, a bank account in their own name and documented wages, which are the first things auditors check. Lifeline's licence position is [licences held: to confirm].

Do you supply workers with hostel accommodation?

Accommodation is usually provided by the mill or unit, not by the agency. Many spinning mills and garment exporters in Tiruppur, Coimbatore and Dindigul run worker hostels. If you offer one, tell us the facilities and rules, and we explain them to candidates before they travel. Workers must be free to come and go and keep their own documents.

Do you work on piece-rate or daily-wage terms?

We work with the wage system your unit already uses, whether monthly, daily or piece rate. Whatever the method, a worker's earnings for normal hours must not fall below the Tamil Nadu minimum wage for the relevant textile or garment schedule (TN Labour Department, as of Nov 2026). Our service charge is [Lifeline's fee: to confirm], billed in addition to wages and statutory costs.

How do you reduce workers leaving after a few weeks?

We explain take-home pay, overtime, food and hostel rules before joining, because surprises cause most early exits. For units without hostels, we prefer candidates from nearby villages and towns. Replacement terms for workers who leave early are [replacement terms: to confirm]. Inside the unit, a fair supervisor and wages paid on time do most of the retention work.
